etymologies.etymologyHTML: A calque of Latin locus commūnis, referring to a generally applicable literary passage, itself a calque of Ancient Greek κοινὸς τόπος (koinòs tópos).

definitions.definition: Ordinary; not having any remarkable characteristics.

quote.citation: 1824, Sir Walter Scott, chapter 7, in St. Ronan's Well:
quote.text: "This Mr. Tyrrel," she said, in a tone of authoritative decision, "seems after all a very ordinary sort of person, quite a commonplace man."

quote.citation: 1897 December (indicated as 1898), Winston Churchill, chapter I, in The Celebrity: An Episode, New York, N.Y.: The Macmillan Company; London: Macmillan & Co., Ltd., →OCLC:
quote.text: In the old days, to my commonplace and unobserving mind, he gave no evidences of genius whatsoever. He never read me any of his manuscripts, […], and therefore my lack of detection of his promise may in some degree be pardoned.

quote.citation: 1911, Joseph Conrad, chapter 1, in Under Western Eyes:
quote.text: I could get hold of nothing but of some commonplace phrases, those futile phrases that give the measure of our impotence before each other's trials.

quote.citation: 1899, Stephen Crane, chapter 17, in Active Service:
quote.text: Finally he began to mutter some commonplaces which meant nothing particularly.

quote.citation: 1910, Elinor Glyn, chapter 4, in His Hour:
quote.text: And something angered Tamara in the way the Prince assisted in all this, out-commonplacing her friend in commonplaces with the suavest politeness.

definitions.definition: Something that is ordinary; something commonly done or occurring.

quote.citation: 1834, L[etitia] E[lizabeth] L[andon], chapter XVII, in Francesca Carrara. […], volume III, London: Richard Bentley, […], (successor to Henry Colburn), →OCLC, page 137:
quote.text: It is odd how easily the common-places of morality or of sentiment glide off in conversation. Well, they are "exceedingly helpful," and so Lord Avonleigh found them.

quote.citation: 1891 [September, A[rthur] Conan Doyle, “Adventures of Sherlock Holmes. Adventure III.—A Case of Identity.”, in Geo[rge] Newnes, editor, The Strand Magazine: An Illustrated Monthly, volume II (July to December), number [9], London: […], page 248, column 1:
quote.text: "MY dear fellow," said Sherlock Holmes, as we sat on either side of the fire in his lodgings at Baker-street, "life is infinitely stranger than anything which the mind of man could invent. We would not dare to conceive the things which are really mere commonplaces of existence. […]"

quote.citation: 1988 December 19, William Styron, “Why Primo Levi Need Not Have Died”, in The New York Times‎[1], →ISSN:
quote.text: The smallest commonplace of domestic life, so amiable to the healthy mind, lacerates like a blade.

quote.citation: 2019, Li Huang, James Lambert, “Another Arrow for the Quiver: A New Methodology for Multilingual Researchers”, in Journal of Multilingual and Multicultural Development, →DOI, page 4:
quote.text: Collecting data via transects is a commonplace in biology[.]

definitions.definition: A memorandum; something to be frequently consulted or referred to.

quote.citation: 1710, Jonathan Swift, A Discourse concerning the Mechanical Operation of the Spirit:
quote.text: Whatever, in my reading, occurs concerning this our fellow creature, I do never fail to set it down by way of common-place.

definitions.definition: To enter in a commonplace book, or to reduce to general heads.

quote.citation: 1711, Henry Felton, Dissertation on Reading the Classics:
quote.text: I do not apprehend any difficulty in collecting and commonplacing an universal history from the  […] historians.

definitions.definition: (obsolete) To utter commonplaces; to indulge in platitudes.

quote.citation: 1910, Elinor Glyn, chapter 4, in His Hour:
quote.text: And something angered Tamara in the way the Prince assisted in all this, out-commonplacing her friend in commonplaces with the suavest politeness.

quote.citation: c. January 1620, Francis Bacon, letter to the King
quote.text: For the good that comes of particular and select committees and commissions, I need not commonplace.
